method: Read-only Figma Plugin API inspection across nine pages; representative screenshots visually inspected. Contrast measured using sRGB relative luminance and resolved semantic aliases for both color modes. Group opacity excluded, not treated as failures. Prototype reachability inferred from recorded reactions, not a live usability test.
limitations: No live app or assistive technology testing.
No resizing or modifications to original frames.
Ancestor-fill contrast cannot establish all effects, sibling overlays or runtime accessibility.
Solid fill count includes duplicate screens and component instances.
Clipping candidates include duplicate dark frames and prototypes; not unique defects.

handoff.text: Transcribed from code, not invented. Booking transitions: packages/shared/src/state-machines.ts · Event derivation: apps/api/src/modules/events/staffing.ts
Illegal transitions throw IllegalTransition. Money column shows where the escrow sits at that state.
Awaiting your payment to confirm these staff
Client has not paid yet — not confirmed
Job confirmed — check in on the day
Cancelled — refund quoted before you commit
There is no event transition table. staffingStatus() recomputes status from bookings + clock on every booking write. Designs must not imply a client can move an event between these by hand.
1.  DRAFT · CANCELLED · COMPLETED are sticky — returned unchanged.
2.  now ≥ event end AND every booking finished → COMPLETED.
3.  status is IN_PROGRESS, or now ≥ event start → IN_PROGRESS.
4.  occupied = bookings NOT in (CANCELLED, REFUNDED, NO_SHOW).
5.  occupied ≥ headcount → FULLY_STAFFED · occupied > 0 → PARTIALLY_STAFFED · else OPEN.
Recruitment never reopens after start — even if cancellations free capacity.
OPEN PRODUCT DECISIONS — NOT DESIGNED, BY INSTRUCTION
The goal asks these to be flagged rather than invented. Each is a gap between the requested scope and what exists in code today.

"QR" is an unused value in ATTENDANCE_METHODS. There is no scanner, route, or verification anywhere in apps/ or packages/. The real mechanism is a 6-digit ATTENDANCE code. Build QR, or design OTP only?
Event states Published / Recruiting / Upcoming are not real
Published and Recruiting both collapse to OPEN. Upcoming and Live are not stored — IN_PROGRESS is derived from the clock. Rename the design language to match code, or add states?
EXPIRED / UNFILLED / INTERRUPTED do not exist
An under-staffed event simply becomes IN_PROGRESS with fewer bookings, then COMPLETED. There is no expiry job and no interrupted state. Do these need building?
The model is Event → Booking (one per usher). No shift entity, no per-worker shift duration. Treat shift as a synonym for booking, or introduce a new object?
Only 6 NOTIFICATION_TYPES exist. Shift reminders, check-in failure, client cancellation and dispute updates are all requested but unmodelled.
Escrow is under-specified in this goal
Payment is listed as "where applicable", but escrow is the product: 15% commission, 72h hold, disputes freeze funds. Designs will keep money central unless told otherwise.
What exists in this file, and the rules an engineer needs that the components cannot express on their own.
61 base screens · 39 carry more than one state · 132 light + 15 dark + 7 annotation frames
Commission never inflates the client total
The client pays budget × headcount. The 15% comes out of the usher allocation. A ₦20,000 booking is ₦20,000 to the client and ₦17,000 to the usher.
Applying, shortlisting and accepting an invitation all leave the booking at PENDING_PAYMENT. Only a received payment moves it to CONFIRMED.
COMPLETED still holds the money. Release happens no earlier than 72 hours after the scheduled event end, and only with no open dispute.
Auto-completion does not shorten the hold
Eligible bookings auto-complete 60 minutes after event end. The 72-hour release clock is unaffected.
Event status is derived, never set
staffingStatus() recomputes it from bookings plus the clock. No screen may offer a control that moves an event between states directly.
Once the event start passes, a cancellation that frees a slot does not return the event to OPEN.
100% above 48h, 50% from 12 through 48h inclusive, 0% below 12h. No processing fee is deducted from the client refund.
A dispute freezes, it does not resolve
An eligible dispute freezes held funds. A decision for the usher before the deadline still does not release early.
A failed balance fetch is not ₦0, a failed list is not "no results", and a dismissed browser is not a failed payment. Preserve the transaction and offer recovery.
Status never rests on colour alone
Every StatusPill carries a dot plus a text label. Attendance, money and verification states must survive greyscale.
SURFACE-AWARE COLOUR — READ BEFORE ADDING A SCREEN

bg/inverse means "opposite of canvas" — in Dark it becomes white, which is correct for an avatar and wrong for a hero panel. Large contrast panels use bg/elevated (dark in both modes). Small elements that should genuinely invert keep bg/inverse.
Text follows its panel, not the page.
On bg/elevated use ink/on-elevated and ink/on-elevated-muted — they stay light in both modes. ink/inverse on an always-dark panel goes dark-on-dark in Dark mode.
Accent and held money have three variants each.

brand/accent-text (on light), brand/accent-on-elevated (on always-dark), brand/accent-on-inverse (on a flipping panel). Same pattern for money/held. Picking the wrong one is the single easiest way to fail contrast here.
Status colours are tuned for text, not decoration.
status/success, /warning, /danger and /info were darkened so they clear 4.5:1 on their own tint backgrounds. Do not lighten them back for aesthetics without re-running the audit.
Stale is a label, not a dimmer.

Never dim content a person still has to read — a card at 0.6 opacity drops body text to 2.6:1. Say the condition in words (“Showing saved data from 12 minutes ago”), mark the block with a dashed border/subtle outline, and disable only the actions.
A disabled ghost button needs a fill.

Dimming a filled button is safe: its label sits on the button’s own colour. Dimming a transparent button leaves the label on the page background, where 0.35 opacity reads 2.2:1. Give an inert ghost button bg/surface, border/subtle and an ink/muted label at full opacity.
